## Actinic flux on the photolysis grid (`ActinicFluxOptions`) {#sec-ch07-actinic-flux}

### Summary

The photolysis rate needs the actinic flux on the module's wavelength grid. kintera does not compute it: the caller
passes it in. Four helpers build one: interpolation of a tabulated flux, construction from options, a uniform
flux and a solar-like Gaussian for tests.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** $F(\lambda)$ on the photolysis grid, @eq-ch07-actinic-flux-solar for the test spectrum.

**Data.** Wavelength [nm]; flux [$\mathrm{photons\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}\,nm^{-1}}$].

**Placement.** Caller side, before `Photolysis.forward`.

**Activation.** API only: `create_actinic_flux`, `interpolate_actinic_flux`, `create_uniform_flux`, `create_solar_flux`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Linear interpolation, held constant outside the source grid.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $F$, actinic flux [$\mathrm{photons\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}\,nm^{-1}}$]; $F_{\mathrm{peak}}$, its peak value;
$F_0$, beam flux at the top of the atmosphere, normal to the beam; $\tau$, vertical optical depth counted from the top
[-]; $\mu_0$, cosine of the solar zenith angle [-]; $n_s$, number density of absorber $s$ [$\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$];
$\Delta z$, layer thickness [cm]; $I$, intensity; $\bar J$, mean intensity.

### Derivation

**Interpolating a tabulated flux.** `interpolate_actinic_flux` places a flux table $(\lambda'_k, F'_k)$ on the module
grid with the same rule as the temperature interpolation of @sec-ch07-cross-sections (steps 1 and 2 there): linear
between the two bracketing source wavelengths, and, because `interpn` is called without extrapolation, held at the
end value outside $[\lambda'_1, \lambda'_K]$. A table that starts at 200 nm therefore lends its 200 nm value to every
grid node below 200 nm; it is not set to zero, and no warning is given (row K34, see Limits). The helpers never
convert units: the values come back in the units
they went in.

**The test spectrum.** The solar-like test spectrum is a Gaussian centred at 500 nm with a width of 200 nm,

$$
F(\lambda) = F_{\mathrm{peak}} \exp\!\left[-\left(\frac{\lambda - 500\ \mathrm{nm}}{200\ \mathrm{nm}}\right)^{2}\right] ,
$$ {#eq-ch07-actinic-flux-solar}

computed in `create_solar_flux` ({{< code src/photochem/actinic_flux.hpp create_solar_flux >}}), with
$F_{\mathrm{peak}} = 10^{14}$ by default. It is a test spectrum, not a solar model: it is not normalised to any
solar constant and carries no Sun–planet distance, zenith angle or attenuation.

**Check.** `derivation-checks/check_ch07_photolysis.py` interpolates a four-point table on 90–210 nm to five points,
two of them (85 and 230 nm) outside it, and evaluates the test spectrum on the five-node grid of
@sec-ch07-rate.[^ch07-check-af]

```text
[d1] max rel |interpolate_actinic_flux - np.interp (linear, held at ends)|: 0.000e+00 (tol 1e-14) PASS
[d2] max rel |create_solar_flux - F_peak exp(-((l-500)/200)^2)|: 0.000e+00 (tol 1e-14) PASS
```

<!-- equation-check: eq-ch07-actinic-flux-solar check_ch07_photolysis.py [d2] -->

**Actinic flux from an optical depth (atm2d).** kintera's C++ core takes $F$ as given. The Python solver of
@sec-ch09-sources computes it in `compute_actinic_flux_disort`
({{< code python/atm2d/radiation.py compute_actinic_flux_disort >}}) for pure absorption. The derivation of what that
function should return has five steps.

*Step 1, optical depth of a layer.* A layer of thickness $\Delta z$ holding $n_s$ molecules per unit volume of each
absorber $s$, with absorption cross section $\sigma_s^{\mathrm{abs}}$, has the vertical optical depth

$$
\Delta\tau = \sum_s n_s\, \sigma_s^{\mathrm{abs}}\, \Delta z .
$$ {#eq-ch07-actinic-flux-tau}

@eq-ch07-actinic-flux-tau is computed in `compute_actinic_flux_disort`
({{< code python/atm2d/radiation.py compute_actinic_flux_disort >}}). The units close for $n$ in $\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$, $\sigma$ in $\mathrm{cm^2}$ and $\Delta z$ in cm. The code converts a
concentration in $\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$ to $\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$ by the factor $N_A \times 10^{-6}$ (option
`concentration_unit`), and multiplies by the cell height of the state, which must therefore be in cm.

*Step 2, the direct beam.* A collimated beam crossing a surface normal to it with photon flux $F_0$ arrives at zenith
angle $\theta_0$, $\mu_0 = \cos\theta_0$. Through a slab of vertical optical depth $\mathrm d\tau$ its path is
$\mathrm d\tau/\mu_0$, so $\mathrm dF = -F\, \mathrm d\tau/\mu_0$ and, with $\tau$ counted downwards from the top of
the atmosphere,

$$
F_{\mathrm{beam}}(\tau) = F_0\, e^{-\tau/\mu_0} .
$$ {#eq-ch07-actinic-flux-beam}

*Step 3, actinic flux, $4\pi$ and no $\mu_0$.* The actinic flux counts photons arriving from every direction at a
point, $F_{\mathrm{act}} = \int I\, \mathrm d\Omega = 4\pi \bar J$, with $\bar J = (4\pi)^{-1} \int I\, \mathrm d\Omega$ the
mean intensity that the discrete-ordinate solver returns. A sphere presents the same cross section to every
direction, so the direct beam, all of whose intensity lies in one direction, contributes $F_{\mathrm{beam}}$ itself.
The factor $\mu_0$ belongs to the irradiance on a horizontal surface, $\int I \mu\, \mathrm d\Omega = \mu_0
F_{\mathrm{beam}}$, not to the actinic flux. With absorption only and a black surface there is no diffuse light, so
$F_{\mathrm{act}} = 4\pi \bar J = F_0 e^{-\tau/\mu_0}$. The code multiplies $\bar J$ by `actinic_scale` $= 4\pi$.

*Step 4, from levels to cells and the layer order.* The solver returns $\bar J$ on the levels between layers; the code
assigns each cell the mean of its two levels, so a cell between optical depths $\tau_{\mathrm{up}}$ and
$\tau_{\mathrm{dn}}$ gets $\tfrac12 F_0 (e^{-\tau_{\mathrm{up}}/\mu_0} + e^{-\tau_{\mathrm{dn}}/\mu_0})$. This is the level
average, not the mean over the layer, which differs from it for a layer of optical depth near 1 or more. The
discrete-ordinate solver counts layers from the top: its layer 0 is where the beam enters. The atm2d state counts
from the bottom: pressure falls with the layer index (`tests/test_atm2d.py`, the state of
`test_actinic_flux_from_disort_supports_2d_state`). So the optical depths must be reversed along the layer axis
before the call and the cell values reversed back after it. The code does neither
({{< code python/atm2d/radiation.py compute_actinic_flux_disort >}}): the beam enters the bottom cell of the state
(S7-3, row K17).

*Step 5, which cross section absorbs.* $\sigma_s^{\mathrm{abs}}$ in @eq-ch07-actinic-flux-tau is the total absorption
of the absorber, the dissociating channels included: every absorbed photon is removed from the beam, whatever it does
to the molecule. By the column convention of @sec-ch07-rate (row K18), that is column 0, so
$\sigma_s^{\mathrm{abs}} = \sigma_0$ taken once per absorber, and the channel columns are not added to it. The code
takes column 0 ({{< code python/atm2d/radiation.py _total_cross_section_by_species >}}). At the pin the KINETICS7
reader breaks the convention: it stores $\sigma_0 - \sum_{b \ge 1} \sigma_b$ in column 0
(@eq-ch07-cross-sections-absorption), so the optical depth of a KINETICS7 absorber leaves out its dissociating
absorption (S7-4, row K18). From reading the code, not run: the pin also adds column 0 of every reaction of the same
absorber, which counts its total once per reaction; both in-tree Chapman decks have one photolysis reaction per
absorber (`O2 => 2 O`, `O3 => O2 + O`), so this is latent in the tree. The in-tree deck `tests/chapman_cycle.yaml` stores the
remainder in column 0 (its O2 row at 100 nm is `[100, 4.43080e-20, 1.11090e-19]`, column 0 below column 1). The K18
fix takes column 0 once per absorber and converts that deck to totals ($c_0 \leftarrow c_0 + c_1$).

**Check.** `derivation-checks/check_ch07_photolysis.py` builds two four-cell columns (height increasing with the
index, as in the state), $\mu_0 = 0.5$ and $F_0 = 10^{12}$, and calls `compute_actinic_flux_disort`.[^ch07-check-disort]
Column 0 holds O2 of `data/chapman_cycle.yaml` in its top cell only; its oracle is @eq-ch07-actinic-flux-beam from the
top with the level average of step 4. Column 1 holds no absorber, so each of its cells sees the full beam whichever
end of the column the beam enters. For step 5 it builds one cell of a KINETICS7 absorber whose file gives a total
absorption of $10^{-18}\ \mathrm{cm^2}$ and channels of $3 \times 10^{-19}$ and $2 \times 10^{-19}\ \mathrm{cm^2}$, with
$n \Delta z = 10^{18}\ \mathrm{cm^{-2}}$, so @eq-ch07-actinic-flux-tau gives $\Delta\tau = 1$.

```text
[i1] max rel |actinic flux - F0| over the cells of the absorber-free column (4 pi J_mean = beam flux, no mu0 factor): 2.220e-16 (tol 1e-06) PASS
[i0] tau of top cell at 150 nm = 1.800; actinic flux bottom->top / F0 = [1.     1.     1.     0.5137]; oracle [0.0273 0.0273 0.0273 0.5137] INFO
[i2] max rel |actinic flux - Beer-Lambert from the top| (absorber in top cell): 3.560e+01 (tol 1e-06) EXPECTED-FAIL  (S7-3)
[i3] max rel |optical depth - n sigma_total dz| for a KINETICS7 absorber, total 1e-18, channels 3e-19 + 2e-19 (code 0.5000, oracle 1.0000): 5.000e-01 (tol 1e-06) EXPECTED-FAIL  (S7-4)
```

`[i1]` confirms step 3: at $\mu_0 = 0.5$ every cell that the beam reaches unattenuated gets $F_0$, not $\mu_0 F_0$.
The line does not depend on the layer order, so it holds before and after the K17 fix. A transparent cell above an
absorber in the same column would not do: at the pin the beam enters the bottom cell, so such a cell sees only the
attenuated beam. `[i0]` and `[i2]` are step 4: the three cells under the absorber should see $e^{-1.8/0.5} = 0.0273$ of
the beam, but see all of it, because the solver puts the beam into the state's bottom cell. `[i2]` is an expected
failure that documents S7-3 (row K17); the in-tree test `test_actinic_flux_from_disort_supports_2d_state` asserts
this reversed profile (more flux in layer 0, at $10^5$ Pa, than in the top layer). `[i3]` is step 5: the optical depth
is half the total, because the KINETICS7 reader leaves only the non-dissociating $5 \times 10^{-19}\ \mathrm{cm^2}$ in
column 0. It is an expected failure that documents S7-4 (row K18); its tolerance allows for the KINETICS7 reader,
which parses values in single precision. With both K17 and K18 fixes applied, `[i0]` gives
$[0.0273, 0.0273, 0.0273, 0.5137]$ and `[i2]` passes; `[i3]` gives $4.6 \times 10^{-8}$ and passes;
`[i1]` is $2.2 \times 10^{-16}$ in both builds.[^ch07-check-fixes] CUDA: not run; unverified.

### Numerical method

`interpolate_actinic_flux` ({{< code src/photochem/actinic_flux.hpp interpolate_actinic_flux >}}) calls `interpn`
along wavelength. `create_actinic_flux` ({{< code src/photochem/actinic_flux.hpp create_actinic_flux >}}) returns
ones when `default_flux` is empty. Otherwise it returns `default_flux` unchanged when the option's `wavelength` is
empty (its length must then equal the target grid's, or the call is refused), and an interpolation from the
option's `wavelength` whenever that is set, even if it equals the target grid. The options `wave_min` and `wave_max` are stored but not
read by these helpers (from reading the header).

#### Caller contract for a computed actinic flux

A caller that computes $F$ itself, for example from a radiative-transfer model, hands it to `Photolysis.forward` under
these rules. Items marked "checked" raise an error when broken; the others are not checked.

1. Grid: $F$ is sampled on the module's `wavelength` buffer, which is the first reaction's grid in nm
   (@sec-ch07-cross-sections). A flux on another grid goes through `interpolate_actinic_flux` first. The length of the
   first axis is checked; the wavelength values are not.
2. Shape: $F$ has shape `(nwave)` for one spectrum shared by every cell, or `(nwave, *T.shape)` with wavelength first.
   A batch shape that does not broadcast against the temperature fails with a generic tensor error, not a kintera
   message.
3. Units: photons $\mathrm{cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}\,nm^{-1}}$ for the trapezoidal rule, or photons
   $\mathrm{cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$ per bin with `quadrature_weights`. Not checked; nothing is converted.
4. Values: negative and non-finite values are not checked. A negative flux gives a negative $J$ and a NaN gives a NaN
   rate.
5. Order: `update_xs_diss_stacked(T)` after every change of $T$, then `forward(T, F)`. An empty cache is refused; a
   cache built for another temperature shape fails with a generic reshape error; a cache built for other temperature
   values of the same shape is used without a check (from reading `forward`, not run).
6. Optical depth, solar zenith angle and the conversion of mean intensity to actinic flux are outside kintera's C++
   core. The Python solver of @sec-ch09-sources does them in `compute_actinic_flux_disort`
   ({{< code python/atm2d/radiation.py compute_actinic_flux_disort >}}), derived in steps 1–5 of the Derivation.
   At the pin it gets the zenith angle and the factor $4\pi$ right (check line `[i1]`), but hands the layers to the
   solver bottom-first, so the flux profile is upside down (check line `[i2]`, S7-3, row K17), and for a KINETICS7
   absorber its optical depth leaves out the dissociating absorption, because the reader does not keep the total in
   column 0 (check line `[i3]`, S7-4, row K18). A caller should not use its result as a correct actinic flux until K17
   and K18 are fixed.

Items 2, 4 and 5 were checked by a run against kintera 2.6.5 built from the pin[^ch07-contract-src]. Item 6 is
checked by `[i1]`, `[i2]` and `[i3]` of the check script for the zenith angle, $4\pi$, the layer order and the
total-absorption optical depth; the per-reaction sum and the deck columns of step 5 are from reading.

### Limits

No radiative transfer, no optical depth and no solar zenith angle in the C++ core: all of that is the caller's, as
listed in the caller contract of @sec-ch07-actinic-flux. The Python helper `compute_actinic_flux_disort` reverses the
layer order (`[i2]`, S7-3, row K17), and for a KINETICS7 absorber its optical depth misses the dissociating
absorption (`[i3]`, S7-4, row K18). All of this was run on CPU only; CUDA is unverified.

- A flux table is held at its end values outside its own range rather than set to zero, without a warning: a table of
  $10^{13}$ on 200–700 nm placed on a 100–320 nm grid makes $J(\mathrm{O_2})$ 41.5 times what it is with zero flux
  below 200 nm (row K34).[^ch07-k34]
